headline_marked: [[Case filed against Gazi Salahuddin Tanvir]] for derogatory Facebook posts on PM Tarique Rahman
headline: Case filed against Gazi Salahuddin Tanvir for derogatory Facebook posts on PM Tarique Rahman
summary: Gazi Salahuddin Tanvir, suspended from the National Citizen Committee, faces legal action in Bogura for alleged defamatory remarks against Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Facebook. The posts, made on July 29, 2026, reportedly caused public outrage before bein
details: A case has been filed against Gazi Salahuddin Tanvir, the recently suspended joint member secretary of the National Citizen Committee, over derogatory and defamatory statements about Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Facebook. The complaint alleges that Tanvir's posts intentionally demeaned the honour of the prime minister and compromised national stability.

HS Maftun Ahmed Khan Rubel, president of the Bogura Sadar upazila BNP unit, filed the case on August 2, 2026, with the Bogura Sadar Police Station. The officer-in-charge, Ibrahim Ali, confirmed the filing to The Daily Star, stating that preliminary investigations found the allegations to have merit.

The incident reportedly occurred on July 29, 2026, around 3:00pm, while the plaintiff was at the BNP party office in Bogura city. Tanvir allegedly posted defamatory remarks on his Facebook profile in the context of recent attacks in Sylhet, followed by another provocative post.
The complaint further states that these viral posts created widespread public outrage. Following significant public backlash, the accused later deleted the controversial posts from his social media.
OC Ibrahim confirmed that legal action will now be taken against Tanvir based on the complaint. This development follows the National Citizen Committee's own disciplinary action against him.
The NCP central executive committee suspended Tanvir from his post on July 31 and issued him a show-cause notice, indicating internal repercussions alongside the legal proceedings.

headline_marked: [[Husband remanded in dentist's murder case]] in Dakshinkhan, Dhaka
headline: Husband remanded in dentist's murder case in Dakshinkhan, Dhaka
summary: Md Sohel Rana, husband of the deceased Dr. Sara Roksana, has been placed on a two-day remand by a Dhaka court for questioning in connection with her murder.
details: A Dhaka court has granted a two-day remand for Md Sohel Rana, husband of dentist Sara Roksana, in connection with her murder in Dakshinkhan. The court approved the remand after the investigating officer requested seven days for interrogation.

Dr. Roksana's body was discovered on July 30 in her Fayedabad apartment by her 10-year-old daughter, who found her mother suffocated with a pillow. Initially, it was suspected that a robbery had occurred, as a window grill was cut and gold ornaments worth approximately Tk 20 lakh were reported missing.

However, police investigation began to focus on Sohel Rana. CID collected evidence from the scene, and police noted inconsistencies, such as no one hearing sounds despite a cut window grill. Sohel Rana was detained on Friday night.

In the remand application, police highlighted that shoe prints found on the inner balcony matched Sohel Rana's shoes, which he admitted were his. Crucially, no shoe prints were found on the outer roof or opposite side, casting doubt on the robbery theory.

The victim's daughter also told police that her mother usually locked the door from the inside before she left for school, but it was not locked on the day of the incident. Furthermore, Sohel Rana reportedly did not attempt to touch or provide aid to his wife upon discovering her body, and his personal wardrobe remained undisturbed.

Police believe the scene was staged to look like a robbery, as old, empty jewelry boxes were neatly arranged. Sohel Rana reportedly admitted to long-standing marital discord and suspected his wife of having an affair.

The victim's family has accused Sohel Rana of long-term abuse and having multiple extramarital affairs. Dr. Roksana had reportedly expressed fears for her safety to her sister shortly before her death. Sohel Rana denies the murder, claiming police framed him and demanding a fair investigation.
